title: Experiment: request-time recompilation, and what a rejected document looks like in production
summary: The compiler was exercised from a temporary Server Component route under `next build` + `next start`, serving against a copy of `planning-content`. The route built as `ƒ /probe-mdx`. A stage document containing `<Callout>MARKER_ONE</Callout>` rendered the mapped component as `<aside data-vpw-mdx="Callout">`. Editing that document on disk to MARKER_TWO, with nothing rebuilt and the server left running, made the next request return MARKER_TWO and the edited heading. Replacing the document with `Inline {1 + 1} expression.` made the next request return HTTP 200 whose Suspense slot resolved to a React error digest only — no message, no path, no position anywhere in the response.

facts.contentRoot: a disposable copy; the project's own content was not touched

omissions.reason: ACC-0020's protocol was not run here — no warm-up, no sample, no timing. The budget remains an unmeasured target and TSK-0014 owns it.
The server's stdout was discarded. The diagnostic is presumed to be there because the compiler throws it, but presuming is why this is recorded as an omission rather than as a finding.

notes: ⚠️ THE REJECTION IS LOCATABLE TO A DEVELOPER AND INVISIBLE TO AN OPERATOR, which is the finding worth carrying forward. `StageDocumentRejected` carries the path, line and column; React's production error boundary replaces all of it with a digest, and the response is a 200 because the shell had already streamed. A stage view that simply renders `<Content />` would show a blank region and a success status for a document the compiler refused precisely. ⚠️ That is DEC-0022's rule arriving in a new place: the operator is looking at a browser, and a failure that reaches only the server log leaves the page looking fine. Catching `StageDocumentRejected` and rendering it is CMP-0016's work (TSK-0009), and it is now a measured obligation rather than a nicety.
